text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000067's 99215 billing is concentrated on low-complexity patients well beyond risk-adjusted expectations, but records are too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern points toward upcoding. 99215 share runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as rash (R21), follow-up (Z09), UTI (N39.0) and uncomplicated hypertension (e.g., C0035141, C0035151, C0035056). The documentation does not settle the question: only two 99215 claims came back with records, and they split. C0035057 was documented at moderate MDM with 32 minutes, below the billed level. C0035518 was supported with high MDM and 44 minutes. Both are high-complexity patients, so no low-complexity 99215 has been reviewed at all, and the single data-reviewed note without a lab or test line is only weak evidence of inflated documentation. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, especially the R21, Z09 and N39.0 visits, and check whether the documented MDM and time support level 5."}
